deals.whyRanked: Allegiant's own fare calendar shows $62 one-way BOS-to-TYS (Nov 14) and $46-52 the other direction (Oct 24) — the cheapest confirmed round trip of the week, and the Smokies are a 45-minute drive.
deals.soloWhy: Downtown's compact grid is easy to explore alone on foot, and the Cosby entrance to the park is quiet and uncrowded compared to Cades Cove.

highlights: Market Square street music and farmers' stalls
World's Fair Park and the Sunsphere
Ijams Nature Center quarry swimming hole
Great Smoky Mountains NP's Cosby entrance
itinerary: Day 1 — Arrive, walk World's Fair Park up to the Sunsphere deck, dinner and live music on Market Square.
Day 2 — Rent a car for the Cosby entrance: Albright Grove or Hen Wallow Falls trail, then Foothills Parkway for sunset.
Day 3 — Ijams Nature Center swim and trails in the morning, Knoxville Museum of Art before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: Downtown and Ijams are walkable or a short rideshare apart; a rental car is required to reach the national park.
guide.stayArea: Downtown near Market Square or Gay Street — walkable to restaurants and the Tennessee Theatre.

deals.whyRanked: JetBlue's fare calendar confirms $59 one-way each direction (Oct 14-24, Nov 7/16/26) — the same flat floor as last week — and it keeps the top solo score of the five plus a Shenandoah boost.
deals.soloWhy: The Metro reaches nearly every monument and museum, the Mall is safe to walk solo well into the evening, and the Smithsonians are free.

highlights: National Mall monuments lit up after dark
National Gallery of Art's East Building
Great Falls Park overlook on the Potomac
itinerary: Day 1 — Land, drop bags, National Gallery's East Building before close, then the Mall monuments once they're lit and quiet.
Day 2 — Rent a car for Shenandoah: Skyline Drive to Hawksbill or Stony Man summit, back for an H Street dinner.
Day 3 — Great Falls Park towpath walk in the morning, Eastern Market for lunch before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: Metro covers the Mall, museums, and most neighborhoods; a rental car is only needed for Shenandoah or Great Falls.
guide.stayArea: Near a Metro stop on the Orange/Blue/Silver line (Capitol Hill or Foggy Bottom) for the fastest reach to the Mall.

deals.whyRanked: New pick: Southwest's own fare calendar shows $59 one-way each direction (Oct 14-21, Nov 5-18) — essentially tied with DC on price, a different city, and Southwest's free 2-bag allowance sweetens the basic fare.
deals.soloWhy: The Inner Harbor and Fells Point are flat, walkable, and full of counter-seating spots that make solo dining easy, with a water taxi linking the neighborhoods.

itinerary: Day 1 — Inner Harbor on arrival, National Aquarium, water taxi to Fells Point for oysters at a counter stool.
Day 2 — Fort McHenry in the morning, then a Station North mural walk before dinner in Fells Point.
Day 3 — Baltimore Museum of Art, Lexington Market crab cakes before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: Inner Harbor, Fells Point, and Fort McHenry are covered by the water taxi and a short walk or rideshare; no rental car needed unless heading to Assateague.
guide.stayArea: Fells Point or the Inner Harbor — walkable, close to the water taxi and restaurants.

deals.whyRanked: Holding flat: a fresh deal-blog post this week confirms JetBlue basic economy at $157 round trip, matching last week's flash fare almost exactly.
deals.soloWhy: South Congress and downtown are flat and walkable, live music venues welcome solo visitors any night of the week, and Barton Springs Pool is an easy solo swim.

highlights: South Congress Avenue shops and murals
Live music on Rainey Street and East 6th
McKinney Falls State Park's Onion Creek trail
itinerary: Day 1 — South Congress on arrival, Barton Springs Pool swim at golden hour, live music on Rainey Street.
Day 2 — Rent a car for Enchanted Rock: the Summit Trail loop (about 4 miles) plus the Loop Trail around the base.
Day 3 — McKinney Falls State Park's Onion Creek trail in the morning, East 6th Street food trucks before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: Downtown, South Congress, and the lake trail are walkable or a short scooter ride apart; a rental car is needed for Enchanted Rock or McKinney Falls.
guide.stayArea: South Congress (SoCo) or downtown near Rainey Street — walkable to music venues and the Lady Bird Lake trail.
food: Franklin Barbecue (arrive early or order ahead)

deals.whyRanked: JetBlue still holds flat at $80 one-way each direction (Oct 24-27, Nov 14-18) — unchanged for two weeks — and the Everglades boost keeps it in the top 5 over pricier Denver.
deals.soloWhy: Las Olas Boulevard and the beachfront promenade stay busy and walkable well into the evening, with the free Sun Trolley covering downtown.

itinerary: Day 1 — Beachfront promenade walk on arrival, sunset at the pier, dinner on Las Olas.
Day 2 — Everglades NP Shark Valley: rent a bike for the 15-mile paved loop, alligators guaranteed at the observation tower.
Day 3 — Bonnet House gardens in the morning, Riverwalk stroll before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: The free Sun Trolley covers downtown and the beach; a rental car is worth it for the Everglades day trip.
guide.stayArea: Las Olas or the beachfront — walkable, close to restaurants and the water taxi stops.
